description: Provider-neutral synchronization binding. Tracked manifests contain semantic identities and protected locator/state handles only; raw provider URLs, IDs, credentials, state-store locations, and user-specific filesystem paths are runtime-private.
provider_rules: adapter_id names the provider adapter, not an account or file.
locator_handle is a semantic private-resolution key and must not contain a provider URL, raw provider identifier, credential, or user-specific path.
locator_resolution must be private_runtime_only in tracked public manifests.
Exact provider identity is resolved at runtime from protected state; title or filename search is not an identity mechanism.
local_side_rules: local/bidirectional authority requires an explicit semantic local-side handle; hidden consumer-specific path knowledge is forbidden.
locator_resolution must be private_runtime_only in tracked public manifests.
provider-authoritative bindings with ephemeral materialization may omit local_side because the local copy is not a durable authority.
baseline_state_rules: state_handle resolves to durable private runtime state for this binding; the raw state-store path/provider object must not be tracked.
required_baseline_fields must include binding identity, provider revision-or-equivalent, local content hash-or-equivalent when durable, and verification timestamp.
conflict evaluation recovers the last common verified baseline before comparing both sides.
a bidirectional sync with two pre-existing sides and no recoverable common baseline fails closed as BLOCKED_NO_BASELINE.
local_materialization_rules: ephemeral is the default for provider-backed artifacts.
ephemeral materialization uses an OS/runtime scratch location rather than the consumer repository.
provider-bound writes may clean up ephemeral bytes only after provider read-back verification; pulls may clean up after downloaded content verification when no durable local copy is requested.
persistent mode requires explicit consumer policy and a bounded max_retained_bytes value.
a provider-backed edit must not silently degrade to local-only output merely because local generation is easier.
sync_rules: Provider authority requires a provider freshness check before consuming a cached/materialized artifact.
A provider-bound push/reconcile mutation requires a pre-write provider revision check and post-write provider read-back verification.
A pull may report SYNCED after provider freshness/read succeeds and downloaded/materialized local content is verified; it does not require a provider write.
Conflict detection compares current sides to the recovered last common verified baseline.
If both authoritative sides changed since that baseline, state is BLOCKED_CONFLICT.
Provider-native document formats must be mutated with the provider-native API; raw file replacement is only valid for blob files.
Periodic synchronization supplements checkpoint synchronization; it does not replace before-use and before-write freshness gates.
privacy_rules: Public Git may contain semantic locator/state handles but not raw private provider locators or state-store locations.
Private locator maps, baseline state stores, and OAuth material stay outside Git.
Tracked examples must use synthetic bindings only.
Sanitized tracked receipts omit raw provider locators, private account identity, and private state-store location.
